data.title: Homepage
data.hero_sub: Falling in love with Lake Tahoe is easy. Finding the right home in a market this unique… that's where it gets interesting.
data.reality_heading: Incline Village Isn't Like Any Market You've Bought In Before.
data.reality_body: Tahoe real estate operates on its own set of rules. The luxury segment here is defined by low turnover, high privacy, and a pace that catches outsiders off guard. Professionalism here isn't just about sales — it's about survival.
data.stat1_desc: Luxury homes often wait for the perfect buyer. Patience is as critical as the price tag.
data.stat2_desc: Competition is fierce. Half of all transactions are liquidity-driven, requiring rapid negotiation.
data.stat3_desc: Algorithm-based estimates fail to account for Tahoe's specific micro-locations and lot features.
data.guide_eyebrow: YOUR NEIGHBOR BEFORE YOU EVEN ARRIVE
data.guide_heading: This Is Where 35 Years Makes the Difference.
data.cta_heading: Your Tahoe Story Starts With One Conversation.
data.cta_body: Whether you're buying, selling, or just getting to know the North Shore — start with a conversation, not a transaction.

data.title: Buyers
data.lead: Many of the most significant properties in Incline Village never see a public listing. Grant's network surfaces them first.
data.card1_p: Direct access to properties before they hit Compass or MLS — from generational lakefront homes to ski-in mountain estates.
data.card2_p: Buyer agency that prioritizes your privacy. NDA-backed showings, blind offers when appropriate.
data.card3_p: Tahoe-specific zoning, water-rights, and TRPA permitting handled before they become deal-killers.
data.card4_p: We help with property managers, contractors, IVGID enrollment, and the hundred small things between purchase and possession.
data.headline: Quiet Access to Tahoe's Most Coveted Estates.

data.title: Sellers
data.lead: Selling Tahoe property is personal. Our process is tailored for sellers who care as much about who buys it as what it sells for.
data.card1_p: Off-market positioning that protects your privacy and the property's storyline.
data.card2_p: Selective staging, photography, and a calibrated price ladder — built around comparable transactions, not algorithms.
data.card3_p: Cash-pre-approval verification, intentions discussion, and lifestyle-fit conversations before a single showing.
data.card4_p: Coldwell Banker Global Luxury network places your home in front of the right buyers in Aspen, Jackson, and Park City.
data.headline: A Sale Designed Around Your Life, Not Just the Listing.

data.title: Concierge
data.lead: Our work doesn't end at signing. The Grant C. Meyer Concierge is a private extension of our service for current and former clients.
data.card1_p: Trusted handymen, snow removal, lake-house openings, and seasonal preparation — all on speed dial.
data.card2_p: Country club introductions, Olympic Club references, Lone Eagle, Lakeside Beach.
data.card3_p: Coordination with CPAs on Nevada-resident status, Williams Equity transitions, and trust planning.
data.card4_p: Architects, designers, art consultants, household staff — vetted through 35 years on the lake.
data.headline: Beyond the Closing Table.

data.title: About
data.lead: From a 16-year-old part-time ski instructor at Diamond Peak to one of the most consistently top-ranked Sierra agents, Grant has built his career on a single bet: that knowing your client matters more than knowing the market.
data.card1_p: Born in Reno. Family moved to Incline in 1989. Helped run his grandfather's small fly-fishing outfit on the East Shore — that's where the relationships started.
data.card2_p: JD from McGeorge School of Law, real-estate-focused. Practiced for four years before moving into agency in 2007.
data.card3_p: "You don't sell Tahoe by selling Tahoe. You sell it by listening for what someone is actually looking for, and then quietly finding it."
data.card4_p: Coldwell Banker International Society of Excellence, six consecutive years. Top 1% of Sierra agents by volume.
data.headline: Three Decades. One Lake. Thousands of Conversations.

data.title: Crystal Bay
data.blurb: The state-line gateway, where grand lakefront estates meet original mid-century cabins on wooded lots.
data.hero_sub: The state-line gateway, where grand lakefront estates meet original mid-century cabins on wooded lots.
data.overview: Crystal Bay sits where Highway 28 crosses from California into Nevada, wrapping the northwest corner of the lake. It's the quieter, more weathered cousin of Incline Village — a mix of grand lakefront estates and original mid-century cabins on wooded lots, many held by the same families for generations.
data.take: Crystal Bay rewards patience. The lakefront here rarely lists publicly, and when it does the right buyer is often already on a list. If this is the corner you want, the move is to be known here before the home exists.

data.title: Community Page
data.hero_headline: A Guide to Life on Tahoe's North Shore.
data.hero_sub: Sixteen distinct neighborhoods, one extraordinary lake, and the details that make this corner of Nevada worth the move — mapped out from a 35-year resident's point of view.
data.nb_intro: Tap an area on the map to see its character, or pick a neighborhood below. Each opens its own guide, with the homes currently for sale there.
data.todo_heading: What Living on the North Shore Looks Like
data.todo_intro: Skiing in the morning, the beach by afternoon — the calendar here runs on the seasons.
data.todo1_p: A community-owned ski resort with some of the best lake-view runs on the North Shore — and short lift lines compared with the bigger Tahoe resorts.
data.todo2_p: Incline, Burnt Cedar, and Ski Beach are reserved for residents and their guests — swimming, picnics, and boat access through the summer.
data.todo3_p: The Robert Trent Jones championship course and the shorter mountain course, both run by the community improvement district.
data.todo4_p: Hiking and biking from the village down to the lake, plus the East Shore Trail and Sand Harbor's coves just off Highway 28.
data.todo5_p: Boating, paddleboarding, and kayaking on the clearest large lake in the country, with full-service marinas a short drive away.
data.todo6_p: Captain Whittell's stone lakeside castle south of Sand Harbor, open for docent-led tours through the summer months.
data.quote_text: Ask any local where the lake is best and you'll get a different answer for every month — the cove in July, the East Shore Trail in October, Diamond Peak in February. That's the whole secret of living here: there's a season for all of it.
data.quote_cite: Grant C. Meyer · 35 years on the lake
data.schools_heading: Learning, a Few Minutes From Home
data.schools_body: Incline Village built its first elementary school in 1964 and its high school as the community itself took shape. Today families choose between the local public schools and a handful of private options — all within the village, none more than a short drive away.
data.school2: Private K–8 options within the village
data.school3: A newer elementary campus completed in 2009
data.history_heading: From Logging Camp to Master-Planned Village
data.h1_p: The North Shore began as timber country, feeding the Comstock silver mines of Virginia City. Through the 1800s a narrow-gauge line hauled logs up the mountain to a V-flume — the scars of that era still trace the ridgelines between Mill Creek and Sand Harbor.
data.h2_p: By the early 1900s the lake had become a summer escape. Captain George Whittell bought some 40,000 acres and built a stone castle south of Sand Harbor — the Thunderbird Lodge — where he was known for legendary parties and a private menagerie that included lions and an elephant.
data.h3_p: In the 1960s the Crystal Bay Development Company acquired Whittell's holdings and set out to build a master-planned community. Robert Trent Jones designed the golf course, the name Incline Village was chosen, and the first school opened in 1964 — the framework of the village you see today.
data.living_intro: The practical side of the move — how you get here, what residency opens up, and what the year actually feels like.
data.live1_p:
Reno–Tahoe International Airport sits about 45 minutes down Highway 431, which makes Incline Village one of the more reachable luxury markets in the Sierra.

Sacramento and the Bay Area are an easy weekend drive, and most of the village is only a few minutes from Highway 28 along the shore.
data.live2_p:
The Incline Village General Improvement District runs the private beaches, Diamond Peak, both golf courses, the tennis complex, and the recreation center.

Access comes through an annual recreation fee billed alongside your Washoe County property taxes — one of the things that makes residency here distinct.
data.live3_p:
Incline sits between roughly 6,225 and 7,700 feet, which gives it four genuine seasons: deep, snowy winters and dry, mild summers, with around 290 days of sunshine across the year.

Snow piles up through the winter — well over a hundred inches in a typical year — then gives way to long, clear summers ideal for the lake.
data.live4_p:
The village covers the basics close to home — Raley's and the Village shopping center for groceries, the recreation center and library at the core, and the local public and private schools all within a few minutes.

For specialized care and bigger errands, Tahoe Forest Health System is over the hill in Truckee, and Reno's hospitals and shopping are about 45 minutes away.
